clue.text: Brenda, say, ceremoniously in charge of a champagne bottle?

definitions.text: Brenda, say, ceremoniously in charge of a champagne bottle

blocks.clueFragment: Brenda, say, ceremoniously in charge of a champagne bottle
blocks.note: surface reading: someone called Brenda presiding over the bubbly at a party
setter's reading: Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for the late Queen, who smashed bottles against new ships' hulls to send them off

explanation.surface: A woman named Brenda solemnly takes charge of opening the champagne.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye has long called Queen Elizabeth II 'Brenda'; a royal swinging a champagne bottle at a ship's bow is sending it down the slipway.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who breaks the bottle at a ship's naming ceremony is the one who sets the vessel afloat.

clue.text: (& 11dn.) Take no risk as PA, fly undone, exposes head

indicators.note: the head of a word is its front, so only its opening letter is wanted
something undone has come apart, so the preceding letters are loosened and rebuilt in another order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
the first letter of exposes

explanation.surface: A personal assistant cautiously keeps things covered while his flies are open and he is flashing.
explanation.walkthrough: A fly here is the zip on trousers; the surface imagines an indecent exposure while the wordplay just reshuffles the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To play safe is an idiom for acting cautiously and avoiding any gamble.

clue.text: see 18dn.
Coarse knocking off, which is screamed for all to hear

definitions.text: which is screamed for all to hear

blocks.note: blue jokes are smutty or coarse
to knock someone off is slang for killing them

explanation.surface: Someone vulgarly bumping a person off, with screams that everyone can hear.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition depends on the idiom 'scream blue murder', meaning to complain or shout very loudly.
explanation.definitionFit: In the idiom 'scream blue murder' this phrase is the very thing yelled noisily in protest.

clue.text: Bitter Cyclops interrupts rock group in two places

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something, so the single-eyed letter goes inside

blocks.note: AC/DC is the Australian hard-rock band
the setter Cyclops refers to himself as I
the same self-reference, used a second time

explanation.surface: A sour setter keeps butting into a rock band's set at two separate points.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In two places' tells you the I goes into AC/DC twice: after AC and after D.
explanation.definitionFit: Acidic remarks or flavours are sharp and sour, a common synonym for bitter.

clue.text: Given a transfer by the CIA, so gave up?

definitions.text: Given a transfer by the CIA

blocks.clueFragment: Given a transfer by the CIA
blocks.note: first meaning: subjected to extraordinary rendition, the CIA's secret transfer of suspects abroad
second meaning: handed over or surrendered, as in rendering up a fortress

explanation.surface: Someone spirited away by American intelligence finally caved in and confessed.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb render covers both the CIA's covert prisoner transfers and the older sense of yielding or surrendering something.

clue.text: see 25dn.
As some would say, British land Conservatism yields many rather useless leaders

definitions.text: As some would say, British land

indicators.note: leaders are those at the front, so each word supplies only its opening letter

blocks.note: the opening letters of these five words

explanation.surface: A political grumble that Tory thinking breeds a crop of feeble bosses in Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As some would say' points to Welsh speakers: Cymru is the Welsh name for Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Wales is a nation within Britain, and its own Welsh-language name is the native word used by its speakers.

clue.text: Pisspoor Cheryl Cole dumps harp backing – not much on top

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the harp-like word runs from end to start
to dump is to get rid of, so those letters are thrown out of the singer's name
something piss-poor is a shambles, so the remaining letters are a mess to be rearranged

blocks.note: the pop singer's name, taken letter by letter
a lyre is a small harp-like instrument

explanation.surface: A sneer at singer Cheryl Cole ditching a harpist from her act while wearing very little up top.
explanation.walkthrough: ERYL sits inside chERYL; removing it leaves CH and COLE to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloche is a small close-fitting bell-shaped hat, so the wearer has only a little on the head.

clue.text: Dirty, lousy male snot-rag dropping heroin

indicators.note: dropping something means letting it go, so the drug's letter is lost from the handkerchief word

blocks.note: M is the standard abbreviation for male
a snot-rag is a crude name for a handkerchief
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A grubby man's filthy hankie, with the drugs no longer in it.
explanation.walkthrough: Manky is British slang for grimy or of poor quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Manky is informal British slang meaning grimy, nasty or rubbish, matching both adjectives given.

clue.text: Pussy mad? Not unknown. Finished? – then put on ice

indicators.note: 'not' an unknown means an algebraic unknown letter is removed from the word before it
mad suggests wild disorder, so the letters left are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
x, y and z are the algebraic unknowns
a synonym: over, concluded

explanation.surface: A deranged cat, its business over, gets shoved in the freezer.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something on ice is an idiom for halting it temporarily, which is what a suspended project is.

clue.text: see 2dn.
Extraordinary hard-on, being involved with EU female

indicators.note: being involved means tangled together, so these letters are mixed up with each other

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
F is the standard abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A remarkable erection arising from an encounter with a European woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unheard-of is without precedent, hence remarkable and out of the ordinary.

clue.text: Gulp, it moves a sad, pale PM to form new constitution

indicators.note: a new constitution means a fresh make-up, so the letters are recomposed into a different order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gloomy, wan prime minister swallows hard as he redraws the nation's founding law.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the throat lump that visibly bobs when you swallow.
explanation.definitionFit: The laryngeal bump on the throat rises and falls whenever a person swallows, so swallowing sets it moving.

clue.text: Conservative into "rule bending", which is a pain

indicators.note: into means going inside, so the party letter is placed within the other letters
bending a rule twists it out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of rule, rearranged
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: A Tory getting into the habit of bending the rules is a nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: An ulcer is a painful open sore, so it is literally a source of pain.

clue.text: (& 22ac.)Rejected party brief on our Tony Blair and shits' gushing speechifying

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the first two pieces are read the other way round

blocks.note: LAB is the short form of the Labour Party
Private Eye cast Blair as the Rev. Tony, vicar of St Albion's, in its long-running parody
'the shits' is crude slang for an attack of loose bowels

explanation.surface: A jibe at Blair's New Labour as a load of gushing, foul-mouthed rhetoric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Our' Tony is Private Eye's own: its 'St Albion Parish News' made Blair a trendy vicar, hence REV.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a colloquial insult for someone who talks at excessive length without stopping.

clue.text: Tart gets Jeremy mounting Barlow

indicators.note: in a down answer, mounting puts the first piece on top of the second, so they are joined in that order

blocks.note: Jeremy Vine is a BBC radio and television presenter
Gary Barlow is the Take That singer

explanation.surface: A floozy gets a broadcaster climbing on top of a pop star.
explanation.walkthrough: Each celebrity is clued by one half of his name and gives the other: Jeremy's surname, Barlow's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Vinegary means sour or sharp-tasting, a direct synonym of the adjective tart.

clue.text: "Balls division" is the making of a royal?

blocks.note: Ed Balls, the former Labour shadow chancellor
a ward is an electoral or hospital division

explanation.surface: A rude joke that dividing testicles is what makes a prince.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Edward, the late Queen's youngest son, is a member of the royal family, and several kings bore the name.

clue.text: Lap smeared with epoxy produces fit

indicators.note: smeared suggests letters smudged out of place, so they are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Getting glue all over your lap sends you into a rage.
explanation.definitionFit: Apoplexy means a seizure or stroke and, loosely, a fit of fury, so it matches the noun sense.

clue.text: (& 3dn.) Chances grabbing beach outfit: divided tops, various articles

indicators.note: grabbing means clutching something within, so the first word holds the rest inside it
the tops of words are their opening letters, so each of the two words just before gives only that

blocks.note: betting odds express the chances of something
the sands are the beach
the first letter of outfit
the first letter of divided

explanation.surface: The likelihood of a bikini turning up among assorted beach items.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beach outfit' looks like one thing, a swimsuit; the comma-less phrase splits into the beach itself and a separate word giving only its initial.
explanation.definitionFit: Odds and sods is a British idiom for a miscellaneous collection of leftover items.

clue.text: Death of plonker with erection on grass

indicators.note: an erection stands upright, and in a down answer standing up means reading from bottom to top

blocks.note: a plonker is a British insult for a fool, as is sap
to grass and to sing both mean to inform on someone to the police

explanation.surface: A fool dies in a compromising state on the lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plonker' looks like a crude word for a penis, but here it is just an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: Passing is a gentle euphemism for dying, from 'passing away'.

clue.text: Comments about 'Tone' getting first sign of Socialism?

indicators.note: about suggests turning around or moving about, so the quoted word is rearranged
the first sign of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: the letters of Tone, rearranged
the first letter of Socialism

explanation.surface: Remarks on whether Tony Blair is showing the first hint of socialist leanings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tone' in quotes reads as a nickname for Tony Blair, a running Private Eye joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Notes are written remarks or annotations, a plain synonym of comments.

clue.text: Treacherous, having a big gob

blocks.note: first meaning: full of hidden dangers, like ground laid with snares
second meaning, playful: well endowed in the mouth, since trap is British slang for mouth and gob is too

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is invented for fun: 'shut your trap' means shut your mouth, so a big gob makes you notably full of trap.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means full of pitfalls, and the setter also reads it as mouthy, from the slang word for the mouth.

clue.text: see 15ac.
Disorganised Cameron's second seat lost

indicators.note: second points to the letter in position two of the name before it
lost suggests things gone astray, so the letters wander into a new order

blocks.note: the second letter of Cameron
taken as written

explanation.surface: A shambolic David Cameron has lost his secondary constituency in Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at sea is an idiom for being confused and without direction, much like being muddled.

clue.text: Glass top reels around hole which balls may enter

indicators.note: something that reels around staggers and spins, so all these letters are spun into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
O looks like a hole

explanation.surface: A drunk, top-heavy with drink, staggers round a hole that balls might go in, like a golfer.
explanation.definitionFit: In football a goal is scored when the ball passes between the uprights and under the crossbar.

clue.text: Mugs might well get fired by them – pathetic Nick Clegg's first to go, embracing Left

definitions.text: Mugs might well get fired by them

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of the surname
to go means to depart, so that letter is taken away
embracing means hugging something within, so the letter for left is held inside
pathetic means hopelessly feeble, so the letters collapse into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of Clegg, to be removed
the possessive's final letter is kept
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Suckers might be sacked by the Lib Dems, with feeble Nick Clegg ousted and the party embracing the left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mugs' and 'fired' look like voters and dismissals; they are pottery and baking it.
explanation.definitionFit: Kilns are the ovens where pottery such as drinking vessels is baked hard.

clue.text: (& 7ac.) Crew girl tainted with bank's gutter activity ending with bang?

indicators.note: something tainted is corrupted, so these letters are spoiled into another order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl in a crew sullied by a bank's dodgy dealings ends up in the gutter press.
explanation.walkthrough: Kerb crawling is driving slowly along a street to pick up a prostitute; 'bang' is slang for sex, and the kerb edges the gutter.
explanation.definitionFit: The roadside pursuit happens at the kerb beside the gutter, aiming at paid sex, hence a sordid activity ending in a bang.

clue.text: Wave and piss off having been shafted by papers

indicators.note: being shafted by something means being penetrated by it, so the other letters are pushed inside

blocks.note: to piss someone off is to annoy or rile them
PP is the abbreviation for pages or papers

explanation.surface: Someone waves and storms off in a temper after being stitched up by the press.
explanation.definitionFit: A ripple is a small wave on the surface of water.

clue.text: Aversion as a consumer when corrupt, pointless Nixon era is before one

indicators.note: pointless means lacking a point, so a compass-point letter is removed
corrupt means debased, so the letters are spoiled into another order

blocks.note: taken as written
a means one

explanation.surface: A dislike of consumerism during the crooked, aimless Nixon years.
explanation.walkthrough: N (north) is the compass point dropped from the two in Nixon; 'consumer' means an eater, not a shopper.
explanation.definitionFit: Anorexia is a loss of appetite, a refusal of food by the one who would be eating it.
